items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: I do remember hearing Jack Teagarden for the first time. It was on one of the Red Nichols records. ... I felt a great deal of admiration and respect for him.

ctx.x: Were you in some way pulling things together from the variety of contributors to fit the direction that you had? Did you edit things then?

Well, yeah, to some degree I think I did. I'm pretty sure I did, because -- and when I didn't, I was being shoved and pushed around by the powers that be at Decca, because they really knew what they wanted, and I learned a great deal from their operation, Jack and particularly Dave Kapp. Because Dave was the guy that used to take the truck out, the sound truck, and go into the South and try to discover folk and blues and people, and do it right on the spot. And he had a goodly supply and an unlimited kind of…
